AI is rapidly changing the workflows and documentation of production planning and clerical work, but people still carry on-site judgment and professional experience. This article explains the specific impact and response paths.

It does not suit people who fear disorder, cannot tolerate delivery pressure, or dislike data and systems. The job often involves firefighting and delivery accountability, making carelessness painful.

A common path is: start in materials / order tracking → planning assistant → independently schedule production → manage production-line planning → become a production supervisor or move into supply chain.
This career suits careful, resilient, coordination-oriented people who are comfortable with numbers. If on-time delivery is your standard, you can succeed in this field.

Production Planning and Expediting Clerks coordinate production scheduling, material follow-up, and delivery performance. They use ERP to coordinate workshops, procurement, and warehousing and ensure orders ship on time.

paragraphs: Early in the morning, pull material-shortage and overdue lists and prioritize critical orders. During the morning, confirm arrivals with procurement, review capacity with the workshop, and revise schedules. At midday, handle rush orders and exceptions and adjust priorities. In the afternoon, track progress, issue daily reports, and resolve missing-part emergencies. Before leaving, finalize tomorrow's plan and prepare for the delivery meeting.

In one line: align orders with production lines. Duties include scheduling, expediting materials, tracking progress, coordinating workshops and procurement, and protecting delivery dates. The role uses both analysis and communication on the delivery front line.

AI will not replace production planning clerks, but it will reduce standard roles. APS and automated order tracking accelerate routine scheduling, shifting planners toward exception handling, on-site coordination, capacity balancing, and delivery assurance. People who only enter and schedule orders face displacement, while those with shop-floor coordination skills become more valuable.
